prompt:
Solve the following problem as completely as you can.

<problem>
For a prime power $q$, let $v_q=q^2+q+1$. A perfect difference set modulo $v$ is a set $B\subset\mathbb Z$ of residues that are pairwise distinct mod $v$, such that every nonzero residue mod $v$ equals $b-b'$ for exactly one ordered pair $(b,b')$ with $b,b'\in B$. A finite Sidon set is a set of integers whose differences $a-a'$ with $a\neq a'$ are all distinct. (a) Does every $4$-element Sidon set $A\subset\mathbb N$ lie inside some perfect difference set modulo $v_q$, for some prime power $q$? (b) More strongly, for each such $A$, does $A$ lie inside a Singer difference set modulo $v_q$ for infinitely many primes $q$? If so, does the set of primes $q$ for which this happens have positive relative density among the primes?
</problem>

structured_output.text: Answer (from recollection of the literature; full proof not reproduced): (a) Yes: every 4-element Sidon set lies in a perfect difference set mod v_q for some prime power q. (b) Yes: it lies in a Singer difference set mod v_q for infinitely many primes q, and the set of such primes has positive relative density among primes. Sketch: Singer set B_g={b: Tr(g^b)=0}, g primitive in F_{q^3}. A embeds (up to shift/unit multiplier) iff there is primitive g with the four points g^{a_i} collinear in PG(2,q). This is a point-count on a variety over F_q (Weil-type bounds) combined with a character-sum sieve for primitivity; the Sidon condition ensures non-degeneracy/independence of the conditions; the admissible primes are governed by Frobenius/Chebotarev conditions giving positive density. I have not carried out the estimates in detail, and the result is specific to size 4.
